name: Glottis Ltd
title: Glottis Ltd - 544557 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Glottis is a freight forwarder whose revenue rose 39.5% YoY to Rs 2,345m while TEUs fell to 21,841 from 26,278, so growth is price/mix-led, with EBITDA margin 6.9% and no capacity-discipline evidence beyond its own fleet build.

summary.headline: Glottis Q1 FY27 revenue rose 39.5% YoY to Rs 2,345 mn, but EBITDA of Rs 163 mn fell from Rs 169 mn a year ago; margin 6.9%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 39.5% YoY and 19.7% QoQ to Rs 2,345 mn, supported by better realisations and business mix despite lower container throughput. EBITDA was Rs 163 mn (6.9% margin), down YoY from Rs 169 mn but up 54.8% QoQ from Rs 105 mn; PAT was Rs 107 mn (4.6% margin). TEU volumes fell to 21,841 from 26,278 YoY and 31,402 QoQ. Sea exports and air freight gained share, and the own-fleet programme moved to 80 vehicles.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 revenue to exceed FY25 levels.
Margin target: slightly above the Q1 FY27 level of about 7% in the coming quarter.
Backward-integration capex (trailers and containers) to be substantially completed in FY27 using IPO proceeds of Rs 132 crore, fully deployed by end-March.
Containers to be deployed from Q3 FY27.
Top-5 customer share targeted to fall to 15%-20% over the next 2-3 years (from ~29% in Q1 and 30%-33% as cited in Q&A).
capex_capacity: Owned fleet at 80 vehicles at end-Q1 FY27, up from 42 at end-Q4 FY26 and 17 at end-Q3 FY26; 38 vehicles added in the quarter.
Container deployment to start in Q3 FY27.
Capex in Q1 described as minimal; IPO proceeds of Rs 132 crore to be fully used by end-March 2027.
CRISIL monitoring agency report says IPO proceeds used as planned with no deviations.
Plans to expand physical presence in Hyderabad, Kolkata (currently operating office only) and Ahmedabad, which are to become more field-focused.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth came from better realisations and favourable mix, with overall pricing described as competitive.
Operating costs rose with business activity, which pressured profitability.
New customers added: 260; repeat customers about 75% of the base.
Asia about 84% of revenue; North America about 10%, Europe about 3%, Africa about 2%, South America about 1%.
US share reportedly rose from about 4%-5% to close to 10%; management is prioritising Africa, US and Europe corridors.
Industry mix: renewable energy about 13% (call's prepared remarks) / 38% (CFO remarks), consumer durables about 10% (vs 7%), chemicals about 7% (vs 2%), engineering about 8%.
Geopolitical impact (Iran-related conflict) described as minor on price and supply availability, with Far East to India lanes most exposed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of geopolitics on international trade and freight, and mitigation steps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the impact minor on pricing and supply availability, less than seen in other trades, given 84% Asia exposure, and said it is being mitigated.

qa_highlights.question: Growth and margin outlook for the year and next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects revenue to exceed FY25 levels and targets margins slightly above the current ~7%.

qa_highlights.question: Total capex plan and Q1 spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex of Rs 132 crore from the IPO to be fully deployed by end-March 2027; Q1 capex was minimal, with 42 trailers added and containers arriving from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Where will top-5 customer concentration go in 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects it to fall to 15%-20% from about 30%-33%, as the customer base widens.

qa_highlights.question: Strategy for air freight, still single-digit share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said air will give a major boost going forward but declined to give a specific share target for the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: Expansion plans beyond Ahmedabad?
qa_highlights.answer: Hyderabad and Kolkata are priority regions; Kolkata is currently an operating office only, and all three cities are to become more field-focused.

risks_watch: EBITDA was down YoY despite 39.5% revenue growth; volumes fell about 17% YoY, so margin recovery depends on realisations.
TEU volumes down sharply YoY and QoQ; watch whether revenue growth holds without volume recovery.
Geopolitical disruption (Iran-related) to freight rates, vessel availability and supply from Asia.
Execution risk on Rs 132 crore capex, with containers not deployed until Q3 FY27.
Management gave inconsistent industry-mix figures (renewable energy 13% in prepared remarks vs 38% in CFO remarks); the figure needs verification.
Air freight growth is from a small base, and management gave no quantified target.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line growth and diversification, but cautious and vague on margins, air freight and geopolitical impact; several answers were non-committal ('not as much as we expected', 'I can't comment exactly').
key_quotes: The lower throughput was partially offset by better realizations and higher contribution of business mix, higher revenue per shipment.

adds.what: Owned fleet expansion to 80 vehicles (38 added in Q1 FY27), including 42 trailers added in Q1
Containers (backward-integration capex, trailers and containers) to be deployed from Q3 FY27

growth.why: Management expects FY27 revenue to exceed FY25 levels and the owned fleet grew from 42 to 80 vehicles with containers due from Q3 FY27, but TEUs fell 17% YoY to 21,841 and no utilisation or precise revenue growth guidance was given.
